findings.title: Non-finite training loss
findings.message: train/loss became Inf at step 322 (1 non-finite point(s) in this run).
fixes: Inspect the objective and logging reduction separately: an empty batch or empty logging window can produce NaN even while optimizer updates remain finite.
Check for a divide-by-zero or log(0) in the loss calculation.
If the optimizer's loss or gradients also become non-finite, inspect the learning rate, gradient clipping and mixed-precision loss scaling.

findings.title: Loss spike
findings.message: eval/loss jumped to 54.88 at step 320 from a level of 0.1838, 29 times the run's progress, for 1 logged point.
fixes: Lower the learning rate or add/extend LR warmup.
Clip gradients (or lower the existing max-norm).
Check the batch at this step for a data or tokenization bug (e.g. an unmasked pad token, a corrupted shard).
If the level came straight back and it doesn't recur, it may be one bad batch.

findings.title: Loss spike
findings.message: train/loss jumped to 55.49 at step 321 from a level of 0.1953, 22 times the finite segment's progress, for 1 logged point. Assessed within the finite segment at steps 0-321 (322 observations); no loss trajectory is inferred across NaN/Inf readings.
fixes: Lower the learning rate or add/extend LR warmup.
Clip gradients (or lower the existing max-norm).
Check the batch at this step for a data or tokenization bug (e.g. an unmasked pad token, a corrupted shard).
If the level came straight back and it doesn't recur, it may be one bad batch.

findings.title: Evaluation loss rising
findings.message: Lowest logged eval/loss in this finite segment was 0.183 at step 290; the last value is 54.88 (299.9x its minimum, slope diagnostic p=0.0833). (Downgraded: a spikes finding at step 321 explains this rise better than ordinary overfitting does.)
fixes: If a checkpoint was saved near step 290, compare it with the last saved checkpoint on the same evaluation examples.
Check evaluation-data and metric-definition changes before attributing the rise to training.
If the regression persists on a comparable evaluation set, consider early stopping, regularization, or more training data.

findings.title: LR rose after decay
findings.message: lr fell from 0.4 at step 20 to 1.097e-05 at step 319, then rose to 30 at step 322. This can be an intended cycle or restart; the log alone does not establish a scheduler fault.
fixes: If this matches an intended cycle or warm restart, no correction is needed.
Otherwise, check that scheduler state was restored with the optimizer after a checkpoint resume.
Check the scheduler's configured horizon and how often scheduler.step() is called.
